text:
sofia.support: heads-up — customer acme-corp reported SSO break after their IdP cert rotation around 07:12 UTC. Multiple users see 'SAML response signature validation failed' and can't complete login. ticket #INC-8921. They say it worked before rotation. attaching snippet from our SAML logs below.

sofia.support: logs: `ERROR sso: verify_signature failed audience_mismatch=false recipient_mismatch=false reason=signature_invalid cert_fingerprint=unknown`

raj.support: can you paste the raw SAMLResponse (base64) or at least the Assertion Signature block? also which IdP (Okta/Azure/OneLogin)?

sofia.support: customer on Azure AD. they sent metadata XML and we pulled it earlier, but they rotated cert and uploaded new metadata this morning. here's their KeyDescriptor block they emailed: ```<KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\"><KeyInfo><X509Data><X509Certificate>MIIC...OLDCERT...</X509Certificate></X509Data></KeyInfo></KeyDescriptor><KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\"><KeyInfo><X509Data><X509Certificate>MIIC...NEWCERT...</X509Certificate></X509Data></KeyInfo></KeyDescriptor>``` they have two KeyDescriptor entries (old then new).

jamie.saml-eng: quick checklist: 1) confirm which certificate we attempted to validate against (our logs didn't show fingerprint). 2) check if our metadata cache still has old metadata or was refreshed. 3) confirm ACS URL / SP EntityID match exactly (trailing slash matters).

sofia.support: i grepped the metadata cache for acme-corp; our cached fetched_at=2024-11-20T06:50:03Z (before rotation). but we did a metadata refresh job at 07:00 that should have pulled the new XML. job logs show http 200 and saved, but the parsed cert list only includes the old cert. weird.

deploy-bot: metadata-refresh-job(07:00): fetch https://login.microsoftonline.com/acme/metadata/2007-06/federationmetadata.xml 200 OK saved to /var/cache/saml/acme/1769123.meta fetched_at=2024-11-20T07:00:12Z

raj.support: maybe Azure returns a multipart metadata or signs the metadata and we only parsed first KeyDescriptor? Does our parser assume single KeyDescriptor? jamie?

jamie.saml-eng: looking at code: saml/metadata_parser.py: we take all KeyDescriptor elements but store them into a dict keyed by certificate subject; however validation path picks the first matching cert in the KeyDescriptor list for 'signing' use. if order is old then new, and assertion is signed with new cert, it should still succeed because we iterate all. need to reproduce the signature verification failure. can you paste a full SAMLResponse (redact PII) or at least the Signature block and SignedInfo Reference URI?

sofia.support: pasted redacted base64 SAMLResponse to secure ticket link (inc-8921/attachment). but i exported the decoded Assertion and see this SignedInfo: `<SignatureValue>AbCd...==</SignatureValue>` and `KeyInfo/X509Data/X509Certificate` inside the metadata was not included in the response — the IdP didn't embed the cert in the assertion, only referenced it via metadata.

jamie.saml-eng: ok. then the SP must fetch the cert from metadata. hypothesis: our parser is incorrectly trimming whitespace/newlines from the cert and failing to construct a valid x509 object for the new cert (maybe newline differences between PEM vs raw base64). or the new cert's encoding uses `\n` vs `\r\n` and our base64 decoder rejects padding. send me the raw metadata XML file you saved.

sofia.support: uploaded metadata XML to the ticket. also noticing their SP EntityID in our config is `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs` but their Assertion's Recipient is `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/` (extra trailing slash). we had a note that our ACS matching is strict equality. that could cause recipient_mismatch in logs earlier. however the logged reason was signature_invalid not recipient_mismatch.

jamie.saml-eng: two independent issues then: trailing slash causes recipients not to match and we'd reject before signature validation sometimes. but since logs show signature_invalid, focus on cert parsing. i'll run a local parse of the uploaded XML.

jamie.saml-eng: quick findings: the new certificate in their metadata includes whitespace inside the base64 block — Azure sometimes line-wraps at 64 chars but our parser expects a no-newline string. patched a local script to normalize whitespace and decode — it decodes fine and x509 fingerprint matches the one customer provided in their email. reproducing signature verify with python-saml lib against the new cert fails though — digging deeper.

jamie.saml-eng: aha — the IdP metadata has two <KeyDescriptor> entries but the first has <KeyName>old-key</KeyName> and the second <KeyName>new-key</KeyName>. our selection code picks KeyDescriptor by keyName first if present, and for this customer the old-key matched a cached alias so we picked the old cert despite the new cert being present. so signature verification tried the old cert and failed. that's a logic bug: selection should attempt all signing keys if verification fails.

raj.support: can we hotfix to fall back to trying all signing keys when verification fails? and also ensure metadata refresh overwrites cache properly?

jamie.saml-eng: yes. plan: 1) push small change to saml/validator.py to try all signing keys when first attempt fails (handled in 1-line change + unit test). 2) add extra logging to include attempted cert fingerprint on verification failure. 3) deploy to staging and run customer test. I'll open PR and tag for expedited review.

deploy-bot: PR #4512 opened by jamie.saml-eng: "saml: fallback to all signing KeyDescriptors on verify failure" — CI ok, reviewers requested.

sofia.support: meanwhile raj, can you ask customer to confirm ACS URL exactly matches configured SP EntityID? ask them to try without trailing slash or add both variants to their SP config if possible. also ask them to flush IdP session and retry incognito.

raj.support: will do. messaging customer now: "We're rolling an expedited fix; meanwhile please verify your SP ACS/EntityID matches exactly (with/without trailing slash) and confirm the fingerprint of the cert shown in your Azure portal matches the 'NEWCERT' value in the metadata you uploaded. Also, please clear browser sessions and retry."

sofia.support: customer replied: they confirmed Azure metadata shows NEWCERT fingerprint `3A:7F:...:B2` and they confirmed the ACS in Azure is `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/` (trailing slash). they said they can't change ACS easily -> asked us to accept both variants.

jamie.saml-eng: ok i'll include a tolerant ACS match for trailing slash variants (we'll keep strict by default but allow equivalent normalization in login flow). pushing PR change includes that normalization.

deploy-bot: PR #4513 opened by jamie.saml-eng: "saml: normalize ACS/Recipient trailing slashes for recipient check (opt-in)" — CI ok.

jamie.saml-eng: both PRs reviewed and merged to hotfix branch. deploying to staging now.

deploy-bot: deploy hotfix/saml-4512-4513 to staging started at 2024-11-20T08:12:00Z.

jamie.saml-eng: staged build up, running integration test with the customer's metadata and SAMLResponse from the ticket. verification now passes locally when trying new cert (fallback behavior works) and recipient normalization matches.

sofia.support: told customer to test — they responded "login succeeded for edge user" and then "all affected users back online, looks good".

jamie.saml-eng: will schedule a small production deploy with oncall + runbook. postmortem item: add metadata-refresh validation to alert when parsed certs change (we missed that). also add telemetry to log cert fingerprints and which KeyDescriptor was used.

sofia.support: marking ticket resolved, documenting root cause: selection logic preferred keyName/cached alias and did not attempt other KeyDescriptor entries; combined with ACS trailing-slash mismatch caused some failures. mitigation done (hotfix + normalization) and follow-ups assigned to eng-saml to improve parser robustness and metadata-change alerts.

raj.support: thanks all. labeling INC-8921 resolved and notifying accounts team so they can close customer loop. :white_check_mark:
